sub: Training volume is not the input most people think it is. Below a threshold nothing adapts; above it, recovery becomes the limit. Four sessions sit on the useful side of both.

ranked.name: Frequency over duration
lines: Three to four sessions a week clears the adaptation threshold for most untrained adults. A fifth adds load without adding signal, and it is the first thing to go when a week gets busy.

ranked.name: Intensity distribution
lines: Roughly eighty per cent easy, twenty per cent hard. The common failure is the middle: sessions run too hard to recover from and too easy to drive change.

ranked.name: Progression rate
lines: Volume rises when the current volume stops feeling hard, not on a fixed schedule. A calendar-driven increase is how most people meet their first injury.
Four sessions, held for a year,
beat seven held for a month.
points: Pick the four you can keep in a bad week.
Keep the easy sessions genuinely easy.
Raise volume only when the current load feels routine.
